speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry will consider regulations to (i) strengthen recruitment and hiring practices by employers; (ii) ensure employers acknowledge and inform job applicants on whether they are successful in their job applications; and (b) whether the public sector can take the lead in this.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, the guidelines make it clear that job advertisements should not be discriminatory and interviewers should confine questions to those relevant to the job requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Where warranted, cases are referred to the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) for investigation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The Standards detail verifiable progressive actions that companies commit to undertake.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Jobseekers will also be able to identify progressive companies and organisations which publicly adopt the Standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Therefore, employers have an incentive to adopt the Standards even if there are no regulations which require them to.

speaker: The Second Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: However, the tripartite partners agree that the Standard can be updated over time as companies make progress.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: For the acknowledgment of the application, I have received feedback, particularly for those who are taking up public sector positions through Careers@Gov and so on, one suggestion would be at least provide acknowledgement that they have received the application of the curriculum vitae.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I have been meeting many of these interested Singaporeans who are wanting to take up public sector positions, applying through online platforms, such as Careers@Gov, and they say they do not get a formal reply whether they are even shortlisted for interviews or even rejected.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: So, I think it would be a good practice for the public sector to take the lead on this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think this is a matter of work in progress.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We certainly encourage more employers to come on board.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In following up on this question, are there any specific plans to provide more teeth, such as regulations with regard to TAFEP, over the next five years?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the Second Minister mentioned, there might not be a need to have regulatory changes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I was wondering what are the plans for MOM in terms of teeth for TAFEP, enhancements of TAFEP, to have actually actions being taken by TAFEP, of course.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It is with regard to recruitment practices and TAFEP's ability to take action in future if there are any changes to regulations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One of it, of course, is by making them more aware of the benefits of doing so.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Another is that it is able to look into complaints that are levelled against certain employers and refer them to MOM for investigations if warranted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Through this process, TAFEP will either work with the employers to change their practices and, if the employers are not cooperative, to find other means of pushing the employers to change their practices.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is something that we will continue to explore better ways of doing.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But bear in mind that, firstly, there are laws in existence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, all of these measures are available to us.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is not always the case that you have to come down hard on the employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some cases, a combination of persuasion and finding the right incentives for them to do so may work better.
